_meta.indication: Treatment of adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with hematopoietic stem cell transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy (TA-TMA).

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents.
pivotal_trials.phase: Single-arm, externally controlled clinical investigation (adequate and well-controlled).
pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, multicenter, open-label trial of narsoplimab in adult TA-TMA patients, with control provided by a historical comparator rate in untreated patients from the literature.
pivotal_trials.population: 28 adult patients with TA-TMA that persisted at least 2 weeks following modification/discontinuation of calcineurin inhibitors or at least 30 days after transplantation, with platelet count <150,000/uL and evidence of microangiopathic hemolysis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint: proportion of TA-TMA patients who responded (TMA response), defined as improvement in both laboratory TMA markers (LDH and platelet counts) and either improvement in organ function or independence from transfusions.
pivotal_trials.result: 17 of 28 patients (61%; 95% CI: 40.6, 78.5) achieved a TMA response, compared to a historic response rate of 23.3% (95% CI: 15.1, 34.2) based on 149 untreated TA-TMA patients from the literature.

key_safety: Serious infections were reported in 36% (10/28) of TA-TMA patients. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 61% of patients; fatal adverse reactions occurred in 7%, including neutropenic sepsis and septic shock. Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) were viral infections, sepsis, hemorrhage, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, neutropenia, pyrexia, fatigue, and hypokalemia.
target_moa: Narsoplimab-wuug inhibits MASP-2, the effector enzyme of the lectin pathway of complement, blocking lectin-dependent activation of C3 and C4 without affecting the classical and alternative pathways; in TA-TMA this is thought to prevent lectin pathway-mediated endothelial cell injury in small blood vessels.
modality: mAb — a recombinant human IgG4 monoclonal antibody.

rems.type: No REMS; narsoplimab inhibits MASP-2 in the lectin pathway and does not affect the alternative pathway, unlike other complement inhibitors that carry a REMS due to encapsulated-organism infection risk.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; no issues were identified that would have benefitted from public discussion with external experts.

summary.text: BLA 761152 for narsoplimab-wuug (a MASP-2 inhibitor mAb) had breakthrough therapy designation (April 26, 2018) and orphan drug designation (October 22, 2018) for HSCT-TMA. The original BLA (submitted November 17, 2020) received a Complete Response Letter on October 15, 2021 for failing to demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness; the resubmission (received March 26, 2025) was granted Priority review and approved December 23, 2025.

citations.quote: On April 26, 2018, breakthrough therapy designation was granted for OMS721 for the treatment of patients with HSCT-TMA.

The Applicant received Orphan Drug Designation for hematopoietic stem cell transplant associated thrombotic microangiopathy on October 22, 2018 and thus is exempt from Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) requirements.
The basis of the CR was that the data submitted as part of the original BLA failed to demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness for narsoplimab for the proposed indication.
